hyperedges.label: One wire contract across all implementations

nodes.label: Persistent outbound tunnel
nodes.rationale: The sidecar dials out so tenant backends need no inbound port or public IP.

nodes.label: Permanent asymmetric version skew
nodes.rationale: Tenants upgrade sidecars independently of the proxy, so the wire schema must anticipate old clients.

nodes.label: Versioned wire schema
nodes.rationale: The wire schema is treated as the only irreversible artifact; work is ordered by reversibility.

nodes.label: Three protocol primitives
nodes.rationale: Most requested protocols differ only in method or content type; protocol fidelity matters more than protocol-specific code.

nodes.label: Frame-shaped streaming tunnel
nodes.rationale: Frames with stream IDs avoid whole-message aggregation and head-of-line blocking.

nodes.label: Refuse, never degrade
nodes.rationale: A capability mismatch must yield an explicit refusal so round-robin selection does not make identical requests behave differently.

nodes.label: Contract-first development
nodes.rationale: Adversarial conformance fixtures precede the implementation they gate.

nodes.label: Tenant scoping
nodes.rationale: Tenant keys and acting-principal signatures structurally enforce isolation.

nodes.label: Documentation vault gates
nodes.rationale: Documentation claims are mechanically checked because a rule without a gate cannot be relied upon.

nodes.label: Conformance suite as contributor on-ramp
nodes.rationale: A portable suite lets outside contributors implement a sidecar in another language.

nodes.label: Fast tier ten-second budget
nodes.rationale: Fast feedback keeps authors from substituting cheap assertions for meaningful tests.

nodes.label: Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off
nodes.rationale: The sign-off attests contribution provenance rather than transferring rights.

nodes.label: Shared Go lint configuration
nodes.rationale: One configuration prevents Go modules from drifting toward inconsistent checks.

nodes.label: Narrow test lint exclusions
nodes.rationale: Test code may relax complexity checks, but unchecked errors remain disallowed.

nodes.label: Vault check workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs every vault gate on pushes and pull requests with full history and a pinned OpenSpec CLI.

nodes.label: Security scan workflow
nodes.rationale: A weekly scan finds newly published vulnerabilities even if repository code has not changed.

nodes.label: Dependabot auto-merge workflow
nodes.rationale: Only patch updates can merge unattended; changes to the versioned contract require human review.

nodes.label: Scheduled gates and parity checks
nodes.rationale: Scheduled runs detect drift caused by external changes between repository commits.

nodes.label: Conformance suite
nodes.rationale: Executable adversarial fixtures and a requirement coverage report are the intended authority on the wire contract.

nodes.label: Outbound sidecar architecture
nodes.rationale: The sidecar dials out so tenant backends need no inbound port, public IP, or firewall change.

nodes.label: Permanent asymmetric version skew
nodes.rationale: The proxy is operator deployed while tenants deploy sidecars on their own schedule, possibly never.

nodes.label: Wire schema irreversibility
nodes.rationale: An old pinned sidecar cannot benefit from a future wire schema correction; sort work by reversibility.

nodes.label: Three protocol primitives
nodes.rationale: Many named protocols differ only by content type and method token.

nodes.label: Contract-first implementation
nodes.rationale: Freeze schema, then build the streaming spine and breadth; adversarial conformance fixtures precede code.

nodes.label: Suite latency as correctness control
nodes.rationale: Slow feedback encourages assertions that are cheap to satisfy rather than assertions that prove intended behavior.

nodes.label: Gated rule
nodes.rationale: A check fails the build today.

nodes.label: Gate planned rule
nodes.rationale: An obligation whose check is not built yet.

nodes.label: Preference rule
nodes.rationale: Taste quarantined from blocking objection.

nodes.label: Sidecar program
nodes.rationale: A tenant operated program must be self describing and diagnosable locally because the proxy operator cannot upgrade it or inspect its machine.

nodes.label: Locally configured backend origin
nodes.rationale: Received requests cannot choose the origin; path remainder is validated before connection to protect loopback backends.

nodes.label: Key custody
nodes.rationale: A closed inventory prevents cryptographic material without rotation authority, destruction path, or incident location.

nodes.label: Installation trust boundary
nodes.rationale: Material never crosses the tunnel and no interface returns a private key.

nodes.label: Packaging
nodes.rationale: Stopped artifacts must declare what they require and support so a pairing can be judged before deployment.

nodes.label: Custom domains
nodes.rationale: Hostname ownership verification gates service and certificate issuance because a wrongly issued public certificate cannot be undone by a rollback.

nodes.label: HTTP fidelity
nodes.rationale: Separate phase bounds and a response-head commit point preserve long streams and make failures distinguishable.

nodes.label: Edge hygiene
nodes.rationale: Framing, client identity, and authority are derived at the client-facing connection; each hop regenerates its own framing.

nodes.label: WebSocket
nodes.rationale: A frame stream has no natural end, so admission, liveness, buffering, and close causes require separate bounds.

nodes.label: Wire contract
nodes.rationale: Permanent asymmetric version skew makes the wire schema irreversible; frames with stream identifiers enable multiplexing and streaming.

nodes.label: Tunnel listener
nodes.rationale: The pre-authentication window needs its own bounds and must identify the endpoint before credentials are offered.

nodes.label: Conformance suite
nodes.rationale: Third-party implementations require independent, wire-level verification, including deliberately broken implementations.

nodes.label: Sidecar registry
nodes.rationale: A registry entry represents one tunnel incarnation; capability filtering precedes selection across the installation.

nodes.label: Tenant isolation
nodes.rationale: Tenancy is encoded in data and operation signatures so a caller cannot omit the boundary.

nodes.label: Schema migration
nodes.rationale: Rolling upgrades create durable-state version skew; correctness is owed at every intermediate migration step.

nodes.label: Observability
nodes.rationale: Signal delivery and installation-wide, instance-attributed answers make stuck tunnels diagnosable.

nodes.label: Mount points
nodes.rationale: Terminal mounts make longest-prefix matching unambiguous and yield only a mount and remainder.

nodes.label: Code standards
nodes.rationale: Every code rule identifies its enforcement gate or is marked as preference; gates must be demonstrated to fail.

nodes.label: Knowledge base
nodes.rationale: Documentation is a checked artifact: classification, links, citations, authority, and currency are gated.

nodes.label: Reviewing a change
nodes.rationale: Canonical change-description questions and blocking objections target observed prior defects.

nodes.label: Adding a feature
nodes.rationale: Specifications and adversarial fixtures precede implementation; documentation and verification travel with the change.

nodes.label: Fixing a bug
nodes.rationale: A discriminating failing case is committed and observed before the smallest fix.

nodes.label: Testing discipline
nodes.rationale: Fast feedback and adversarial conformance fixtures help tests reject plausible wrong implementations.

nodes.label: Timeout taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Separately bounded phases permit long-lived responses.

nodes.label: Response commit point
nodes.rationale: After the response head, a failure can only truncate the exchange.

nodes.label: Per-hop framing authority
nodes.rationale: Each connection declares and validates its own framing.

nodes.label: Backend-accepted WebSocket establishment
nodes.rationale: The client upgrade is withheld until the backend accepts and chooses a subprotocol.

nodes.label: Bounded pre-join frame buffer
nodes.rationale: Frame count and octet count both bound buffering before backend connection.

nodes.label: Frame with stream identifier
nodes.rationale: This unit enables concurrent streaming exchanges over one connection.

nodes.label: Capability negotiation and refusal
nodes.rationale: Ability is declared and unsupported requests are refused with reasons.

nodes.label: Observed source
nodes.rationale: Pre-authentication limits use the origin observed from the connection.

nodes.label: Declaration-based skip
nodes.rationale: A test run may skip only based on declared capabilities, separately from failures.

nodes.label: Broken-implementation proof
nodes.rationale: The suite must reject intentionally broken implementations before its verdict is trusted.

nodes.label: Registry entry
nodes.rationale: One tunnel incarnation with version, capabilities, and holding instance.

nodes.label: Tunnel eligibility
nodes.rationale: Capability-filtered eligibility is established before sidecar selection.

nodes.label: Structural tenant scoping
nodes.rationale: Every resource, read, and mutation carries the tenancy boundary.

nodes.label: Installation-wide tenant ceiling
nodes.rationale: Per-tenant limits count across all proxy instances.

nodes.label: Migration decomposition rule
nodes.rationale: Renames, retypes, narrowing, and removals are staged into compatible intermediate steps.

nodes.label: Unknown stored attribute preservation
nodes.rationale: Older instances preserve fields written by newer instances.

nodes.label: Signal delivery
nodes.rationale: Unconfigured destinations cause startup refusal rather than silent loss.

nodes.label: Partial installation answer
nodes.rationale: Diagnostics covering less than the installation are identified as partial.

nodes.label: Terminal mount invariant
nodes.rationale: A mount cannot have children, ensuring one longest-prefix match.

nodes.label: Mount remainder
nodes.rationale: The undecoded path suffix after the matched mount is the backend-request input.

nodes.label: Rule-to-gate correspondence
nodes.rationale: Every rule and gate identify each other so enforcement is discoverable and audited.

nodes.label: Bidirectional documentation currency
nodes.rationale: A note fails if its subject vanishes or its planned subject now exists.

nodes.label: Change-description questions
nodes.rationale: Four canonical questions cover breakage, wire impact, discriminatory tests, and checks.

nodes.label: Review checklist
nodes.rationale: Nine ordered review questions target body, headers, method, streaming, tests, authorization, queues, typed errors, and gate subject selection.

nodes.label: Blocking objections
nodes.rationale: A closed numbered set distinguishes review blockers from nonblocking comments.

nodes.label: Main branch protection
nodes.rationale: PR and eight checks are required for non-admins; administrators are exempt.

nodes.label: Contract-first feature sequence
nodes.rationale: Proposal, spec, design, tasks, failing conformance fixture, code, notes, and verification occur in order.

nodes.label: Prior failing case
nodes.rationale: The failing case exists in a prior commit and identifies the wrong implementation it rejects.

nodes.label: Mutation thinking
nodes.rationale: Tests are judged by whether a plausible wrong code change would fail.

nodes.label: Adversarial conformance fixtures
nodes.rationale: Fixtures include binary bodies, duplicate cookies, ambiguous framing, encoded paths, fragmented frames, streaming, and cancellation.

nodes.label: Fast tier latency budget
nodes.rationale: A fast first tier within ten seconds is a correctness control.

nodes.label: Contributor experience
nodes.rationale: Fast local feedback, a complete dev configuration, and a standalone conformance suite make contributions tractable.

nodes.label: Conformance fixtures as good first issues
nodes.rationale: Bounded adversarial fixtures can land before the implementation they gate.
nodes.norm_label: conformance fixtures as good first issues

nodes.label: Clean-clone development profile
nodes.rationale: A generated .env.example and dev profile reconcile production no-defaults policy with usable local setup.

nodes.label: Body octets end to end
nodes.rationale: Character conversion corrupted invalid UTF-8 and split multibyte characters in the prior attempt; a single binary-safe body path prevents divergent handling.

nodes.label: Dedicated proxied-traffic pipeline
nodes.rationale: Body parsers consumed POST bodies, and divergent pipelines rejected content types in the prior attempt.

nodes.label: Bounded accumulators and overflow reasons
nodes.rationale: Unbounded queues let a slow backend consume proxy memory; count and octet bounds need distinguishable overflow outcomes.

nodes.label: Ordered header-field pairs
nodes.rationale: A map silently drops repeated Set-Cookie fields and loses field order.

nodes.label: Chunkwise proxied-body emission
nodes.rationale: Aggregating the whole body before emission destroys streaming latency and memory bounds, including server-sent events.

nodes.label: Per-hop framing authority
nodes.rationale: Relaying Content-Length after changing body octets creates stalls or truncation; conflicting length and transfer coding must be refused.

nodes.label: Opaque method token
nodes.rationale: Method allowlists made DAV verbs unreachable and independently drifted between proxy and sidecar.

nodes.label: Typed wire error codes
nodes.rationale: Debug term renderings cannot be reliably interpreted by peers and may expose credentials.

nodes.label: Proxy component boundary
nodes.rationale: The operator-run Elixir component uniquely owns tenant-keyed durable state, routing, registry, tunnel admission, and certificates.

nodes.label: Tenant-scoped mutations with acting principal
nodes.rationale: Making the principal part of every mutation signature makes tenant isolation checkable.

nodes.label: Conformance suite boundary
nodes.rationale: An independently runnable suite prevents proxy and sidecar from testing only their own fictions of the wire.

nodes.label: Adversarial conformance corpus
nodes.rationale: Octet-level and failure fixtures are written before code and proved by defective counterparts.

nodes.label: Recording origin and process harness
nodes.rationale: The measuring instrument belongs outside the implementations it measures and observes octets without transcoding.

nodes.label: Versioned contract boundary
nodes.rationale: The wire schema is irreversible under tenant-controlled sidecar upgrades and is the single source of frame shapes and registers.

nodes.label: Generated wire codecs
nodes.rationale: One interface definition eliminates independently hand-written encoders that can each validate their own fiction.

nodes.label: Sidecar component boundary
nodes.rationale: The tenant-run Go sidecar dials out and is the only component adjacent to the private backend.

nodes.label: Sidecar capability declaration
nodes.rationale: Declared capabilities permit explicit refusal instead of degraded fidelity for unsupported traffic.

nodes.label: Terminator component boundary
nodes.rationale: A replaceable contract speaker handles client HTTP/2 and later protocols that the Elixir proxy cannot terminate.

nodes.label: Client-facing stream flow control
nodes.rationale: Per-stream credit at the edge closes the flow-control gap left by WebSocket.

nodes.label: Python gate conventions
nodes.rationale: Gate modules use the standard library, report all violations and coverage, and accept common test flags.

nodes.label: Passing-run gate coverage
nodes.rationale: A green gate must state what roots and subjects it actually covered.

nodes.label: Elixir proxy conventions
nodes.rationale: The proxy quality tools are invoked through one lint target and proxied traffic bypasses middleware.

nodes.label: Go module conventions
nodes.rationale: One linter config and make recipe serves sidecar, terminator, and conformance; tests use the race detector.

nodes.label: Credential scan of tree and review range
nodes.rationale: Secrets removed from the working tree remain disclosed in branch history, so both tracked content and changed blobs are scanned.
nodes.norm_label: credential scan of tree and review range

nodes.label: Combined-diff merge scan
nodes.rationale: Conflict resolutions may introduce credentials present in no parent and need a combined-diff scan.

nodes.label: Dated credential scan suppression
nodes.rationale: A per-line escape is auditable only with a past revocation date and printed path, line, shape, and reason.

nodes.label: Prefix-anchored credential detection
nodes.rationale: Deliberate false negatives keep the gate usable and avoid an entropy heuristic that would be disabled.

nodes.label: Non-disclosing credential findings
nodes.rationale: A scanner must not echo matched secrets into build logs.

nodes.label: Review obligations single sourcing
nodes.rationale: One numbered location for each review enumeration prevents silently diverging copies.

nodes.label: Single source build provenance
nodes.rationale: A single build stamp lets operators identify version, commit, dirty state, and time consistently across components facing version skew.

nodes.label: Ten line duplication threshold
nodes.rationale: The ten line threshold falls below the smallest cited duplicated reconcile block and catches renamed structural copies.

nodes.label: Banned defect classes
nodes.rationale: The named constructs encode defects that shipped; narrow detection favors false negatives over broad checks that would be disabled.

nodes.label: Generate sources before compilation
nodes.rationale: Generation must precede every toolchain invocation, including those outside make, because a checkout lacks generated import dependencies.

nodes.label: Fast tier latency budget
nodes.rationale: A ten second wall clock ceiling keeps feedback fast enough that tests target costly correctness claims.

nodes.label: Recorded red gate debt
nodes.rationale: A preimplementation test stays running while its red outcome and closing task remain visible, with changes in either direction acknowledged.

nodes.label: Three test tiers
nodes.rationale: Tests belong in fast, integration, or conformance according to the subject they exercise.

nodes.label: Module size ceiling
nodes.rationale: A 300 noncomment line limit makes growing responsibility visible while splitting remains cheap.

nodes.label: Top level directory README
nodes.rationale: A directory README guides file placement and links to its boundary statement.

nodes.label: Function size ceiling
nodes.rationale: A 60 noncomment line limit prevents oversized functions and inline templates.

nodes.label: Tests assert intended behavior
nodes.rationale: A test shaped around an implementation defect makes the defect appear intended and blocks later repair.

nodes.label: Wait helpers never repair awaited state
nodes.rationale: A waiting test helper that performs the missing transition gives false coverage for a mechanism that never ran.
nodes.norm_label: wait helpers never repair awaited state

nodes.label: No test uncertainty markers or unconditional skips
nodes.rationale: Unresolved reasoning and unsupported skips conceal failing assertions while making a suite appear complete.
nodes.norm_label: no test uncertainty markers or unconditional skips

nodes.label: No submodules or gitlinks
nodes.rationale: One reviewed repository prevents unreviewed submodule pointer updates from crossing the wire contract boundary.

nodes.label: Conformance suite authority
nodes.rationale: Adversarial, preimplementation fixtures tested against defective counterparts outrank either implementation’s self tests on wire behavior.

nodes.label: No weakened test properties
nodes.rationale: Lowering work factors or disabling protections in tests removes the property the tests need to exercise.

nodes.label: Single Go linter configuration
nodes.rationale: One file used by every Go module prevents silent divergence in enforcement.

nodes.label: Binary asset provenance
nodes.rationale: A tracked origin and terms declaration makes added binary files reviewable.

nodes.label: One to one rule gate correspondence
nodes.rationale: Each rule and gate name each other so failures teach their reason and duplicate enforcement cannot diverge.
nodes.norm_label: one to one rule gate correspondence

nodes.label: Single component boundary statement
nodes.rationale: One ownership note per existing component prevents READMEs and other copies from drifting.

nodes.label: Fast test tier
nodes.rationale: Pure, asynchronous tests without Postgres, network, or sleeps run on save.

nodes.label: Integration test tier
nodes.rationale: Real Postgres and sockets with committing transactions allow notifier delivery to be observed.

nodes.label: Conformance test tier
nodes.rationale: Adversarial fixtures exercise the wire contract against every implementation.

nodes.label: Language conventions keyed on tracked source
nodes.rationale: Conventions notes exist exactly for languages with tracked source; otherwise the guide describes a nonexistent system.
nodes.norm_label: language conventions keyed on tracked source

nodes.label: Failure messages name the consequence
nodes.rationale: Human-facing gate failures should identify location and consequence in a sentence; this is an unenforced preference because linguistic quality is not decidable.

nodes.label: Gate states what it does not decide
nodes.rationale: Passing checks can be over-read as complete coverage, so gate modules should state their limits. This remains an unenforced preference.
nodes.norm_label: gate states what it does not decide

nodes.label: Gate docstring names requirement and defect
nodes.rationale: Opening a gate docstring with the requirement and motivating defect turns a verdict into an explanation; prose quality cannot be mechanically verified.
nodes.norm_label: gate docstring names requirement and defect

nodes.label: Superseded decision register
nodes.rationale: Two unnamespaced decision registers collided. The surviving OpenSpec design register has authority; retired identifiers cannot be reassigned because old citations would become ambiguous.

nodes.label: D30 Durable state in PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: The proxy installation holds durable state in PostgreSQL. The choice is reversible by one operator, but database-enforced invariants demand contended integration tests; the decision also records an assumption previously buried across artifacts.

nodes.label: D31 Out-of-scope declaration containment
nodes.rationale: A change may not declare paths in its own tree out of scope. The prior manifest declaration froze the owner’s specifications unconditionally; containment is decidable but weaker than immutability.

nodes.label: D28 Apache-2.0 licensing of authored tree
nodes.rationale: A root Apache-2.0 license covers repository-authored work. Vendored harnesses are excluded; implementers of the public wire specification who write from scratch lack a patent grant from this software license.
nodes.norm_label: d28 apache-2.0 licensing of authored tree

nodes.label: D29 Discover gate roster and reconcile invocations
nodes.rationale: Gate modules, broken inputs, and rule links already encode the roster. Workflow invocations need a declared counterpart and two-way reconciliation because workflow syntax belongs to the hosting service.
nodes.norm_label: d29 discover gate roster and reconcile invocations

nodes.label: D16 HTTP/2 client edge in v1
nodes.rationale: HTTP/2 is first-release scope, requiring a separate contract-speaking edge terminator because the selected Elixir web server cannot handle the needed client-facing protocol.
nodes.norm_label: d16 http/2 client edge in v1

nodes.label: D20 Multi-instance proxy installation
nodes.rationale: Multiple proxy processes serve every tenant sidecar in v1. Client pinning or redirects would create outages or break non-retryable requests; tenant ceilings must generally be installation-wide.

nodes.label: D4 Elixir proxy and Go sidecar runtime
nodes.rationale: The proxy uses Elixir and the sidecar Go. A Go H3 terminator may follow. An earlier Rust recommendation relied on false WebTransport premises; BEAM fits distributed registry, failover, routing, containment and administration needs.
nodes.norm_label: d4 elixir proxy and go sidecar runtime

nodes.label: D17 Capability scope and deferrals
nodes.rationale: Five ownerless capabilities enter scope and three others are deferred with dependencies named; reserved control-plane namespace and unresolved audit-retention conflict still constrain v1.

nodes.label: D24 Permanent asymmetric version skew
nodes.rationale: The operator updates the proxy while tenants update sidecars on their own schedules. Wire decisions are irreversible, capability negotiation is mandatory, and work is ordered by reversibility.

nodes.label: D23 Contract-first conformance suite
nodes.rationale: The versioned wire schema is the root artifact, implementation types are generated from it, and adversarial conformance fixtures precede implementation. Prior independent tests each validated a different fiction while the wire was broken.

nodes.label: D8 Tenant scoping in keys and signatures
nodes.rationale: Tenant ownership belongs in projection keys and each mutation’s acting-principal signature; relying on individual query filters or writer habits cannot structurally ensure isolation.
nodes.norm_label: d8 tenant scoping in keys and signatures

nodes.label: D25 Multi-tenant platform ingress positioning
nodes.rationale: Platform ingress for many tenants is the product positioning. This makes tenant-keyed projections, actor authorization, blast-radius control and audit foundational rather than deferred.

nodes.label: D21 Rebuild from scratch
nodes.rationale: The prior codebase is read-only, cited prior art because its large suite missed structural wire failures; the rebuild must not treat that suite as an executable specification.

nodes.label: D2 Frame-shaped tunnel exchange
nodes.rationale: Tunnel traffic uses frames carrying stream identifiers rather than whole request or response messages. Frame vocabulary and credit participation are reserved in v1 to avoid splitting old sidecars from the fleet.

nodes.label: D22 — One repository
nodes.rationale: One schema should generate both components and eliminate unreviewed submodule pointer updates.

nodes.label: D19 — v1 tunnel transport
nodes.rationale: WebSocket over TLS on port 443 survives tenant egress controls; framing remains transport independent.

nodes.label: D7 — Timeout taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Streams and watches may have no total duration; each observable bound needs its own owner and reason.

nodes.label: Route class without a total time bound
nodes.norm_label: route class without a total time bound

nodes.label: D6 — Per-hop framing authority
nodes.rationale: Discard upstream framing declarations to prevent contradictory lengths and request smuggling.

nodes.label: D1 — Three transport primitives
nodes.rationale: Protocol-specific handlers diverged; most named protocols differ only in content type and method.

nodes.label: D26 — WebTransport deferred
nodes.rationale: Reserve independent streams and datagrams now so a future QUIC edge does not require redesign.

nodes.label: D9 — Domain ownership before issuance
nodes.rationale: Unverified domain claims could produce publicly trusted certificates for names tenants do not own.

nodes.label: D5 — Dedicated proxied traffic path
nodes.rationale: Framework middleware consumes or normalizes bytes before forwarding, breaking fidelity.

nodes.label: D18 — Generated binary frame codecs
nodes.rationale: Field numbering preserves additive compatibility across language implementations.

nodes.label: D10 — Explicit cited carry-forward
nodes.rationale: Reuse a cited idea without inheriting broken implementation details.

nodes.label: D3 — Capability negotiation and refusal
nodes.rationale: Mixed sidecar versions must not silently change fidelity for identical requests.

nodes.label: D27 — Observability before hot path
nodes.rationale: An emitted event without an attached consumer provides no operational visibility.

nodes.label: Attached metric sink and structured logger
nodes.norm_label: attached metric sink and structured logger

nodes.label: Terminal-mount invariant
nodes.rationale: Terminal mounts make strip-one-segment lookup correct without a trie or tie-break.

nodes.label: Per-request Task.async isolation
nodes.rationale: A private request process prevents late replies from leaking into another request.

nodes.label: Insert-before-evict cache reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Readers see a superset during refresh, never an empty table.

nodes.label: Direct ETS reads with protected tables
nodes.rationale: Read from caller processes without a GenServer bottleneck while reserving writes for owner.
nodes.norm_label: direct ets reads with protected tables

nodes.label: Bounded WebSocket frame buffer
nodes.rationale: Bound both frame count and bytes, then fail explicitly on overflow.

nodes.label: Failure fan-out on disconnect
nodes.rationale: Notify all waiting requests and WebSocket handlers immediately when a sidecar disconnects.

nodes.label: Partial unique indexes for soft deletion
nodes.rationale: Deleted rows should not block reuse of unique values.
nodes.norm_label: partial unique indexes for soft deletion

nodes.label: Named database CHECK constraints
nodes.rationale: Database remains source of truth while changesets can map failures to errors.

nodes.label: Boot-time secret validation
nodes.rationale: Fail fast on missing, short, or development credentials in production.

nodes.label: Purpose-scoped versioned key derivation
nodes.rationale: Compromise of one derived key should not expose all secret uses.

nodes.label: Real-server WebSocket wire tests
nodes.rationale: Actual bytes crossing both directions pin the contract more faithfully than no-op serializers.

nodes.label: Explicit configuration policy
nodes.rationale: Required production settings should fail at startup, with all missing values reported together.

nodes.label: Request body loss before sidecar
nodes.rationale: Framework parsers consume bodies before the proxy reads them.

nodes.label: Binary payload corruption in JSON
nodes.rationale: Byte-to-string conversion and JSON coercion replace invalid UTF-8.

nodes.label: Both reference containers fail to boot
nodes.rationale: Runtime environment contracts drift from image and deployment configuration.
nodes.norm_label: both reference containers fail to boot

nodes.label: Duplicate headers lost in maps
nodes.rationale: Map representation deletes repeated Set-Cookie values.

nodes.label: Buffered body disguised as streaming
nodes.rationale: All chunks are read before one tunnel message is sent.

nodes.label: Single reply per correlation ID
nodes.rationale: Cannot express informational responses, trailers, or aborts.

nodes.label: Single global request timeout
nodes.rationale: Precludes long-lived event streams.

nodes.label: Missing backpressure
nodes.rationale: Unbounded messages feed a serialized sidecar channel.

nodes.label: Actorless cross-tenant token write
nodes.rationale: Token update lacks an acting principal.

nodes.label: Global cache rebuild on tenant event
nodes.rationale: A tenant change scans and diffs all mounts.
nodes.norm_label: global cache rebuild on tenant event

nodes.label: Self-repairing notifier test helper
nodes.rationale: The wait helper reloads the cache because sandbox transactions never commit NOTIFY.

nodes.label: Contract tests against two fictions
nodes.rationale: Phoenix uses a no-op serializer; Go tests marshal a struct production does not use.

nodes.label: Unconsumed telemetry events
nodes.rationale: Events are emitted without a handler attached.

nodes.label: Slow feedback incentivizes weak tests
nodes.rationale: Slow suites make cheap assertions attractive and hide distributed defects.

nodes.label: Unreviewed dependency update chain
nodes.rationale: Automerged dependency PRs trigger unreviewed submodule pointer commits.

nodes.label: Adversarial review of load-bearing conclusions
nodes.rationale: Check recommendations against published APIs and primary artifacts.

nodes.label: Reviewed WebTransport verdict
nodes.rationale: Decision survived while the reason was corrected after browser and draft evidence.

nodes.label: Overturned Rust proxy recommendation
nodes.rationale: A false premise about same-process HTTP/3 termination had excluded BEAM.

nodes.label: Completeness critic
nodes.rationale: A different review question exposed deployment, observability, and contributor-loop omissions.

nodes.label: Obtaining the reference
nodes.rationale: The prior art is only useful when readers can fetch the pinned trees and check cited lines; clone origins remain unverified.

nodes.label: Reference fetch source gap
nodes.rationale: The repository records revisions and verification, but no confirmed source or fetch instructions.

nodes.label: Reference citation verification
nodes.rationale: Verify exact seven-character revisions and sample cited file:line text against those trees.

nodes.label: Prior art is not behavioural authority
nodes.rationale: Obtaining the reference makes audit claims checkable, not the old implementation authoritative.
nodes.norm_label: prior art is not behavioural authority

nodes.label: Threat model
nodes.rationale: Maps eight adversaries and assets to controls in owning specifications; describes planned obligations, not running product behaviour.

nodes.label: Request smuggling
nodes.rationale: Conflicting message framing can move request boundaries across a shared connection.

nodes.label: SSRF through the sidecar
nodes.rationale: A client may try to make a sidecar inside a tenant perimeter dial internal or metadata endpoints.

nodes.label: Cross-tenant cookie scoping
nodes.rationale: Path-separated tenants on a shared hostname can otherwise receive each other's session cookies.

nodes.label: Certificate issuance from an unverified claim
nodes.rationale: Unverified hostname claims can yield certificates for names the claimant does not control.
nodes.norm_label: certificate issuance from an unverified claim

nodes.label: Cross-tenant writes
nodes.rationale: An authenticated principal or unchecked internal caller could mutate another tenant's state.

nodes.label: Open relay via tunnelling method
nodes.rationale: A public client could use the proxy to connect to addresses reachable from its own network.

nodes.label: Compression amplification
nodes.rationale: A small compressed stream frame can exhaust shared proxy or sidecar memory after expansion.

nodes.label: Credential and key custody
nodes.rationale: Readers of stores, interfaces, or logs could obtain secrets, keys, or root material.

nodes.label: Per-hop message framing
nodes.rationale: Framing authority derives from the arrival connection; conflicting indications are rejected.

nodes.label: Locally configured sidecar origin
nodes.rationale: Received request components must not influence the origin the sidecar dials.

nodes.label: Mount-scoped cookies
nodes.rationale: Each Set-Cookie is scoped individually to its mount and hostname; incoming cookies are filtered.

nodes.label: Verified hostname ownership before issuance
nodes.rationale: A claim confers no routing or certificate rights until ownership is verified.

nodes.label: Principal-bound mutations
nodes.rationale: Every mutation takes an acting principal and checks authority as part of the operation.

nodes.label: Edge method refusal policy
nodes.rationale: Bare CONNECT is refused and TRACE answered at the edge; other methods pass through.

nodes.label: Incremental decompression bound
nodes.rationale: Compression is per hop, with a bound on expanded message size and post-expansion accounting.

nodes.label: Key and credential non-disclosure
nodes.rationale: Private material cannot be read from interfaces or recovered from stored credential state.

nodes.label: Operator view
nodes.rationale: The operator deploys a multi-instance proxy and needs installation-wide configuration, observation, diagnosis, and actions.

nodes.label: Multi-instance installation
nodes.rationale: Answers spanning the installation must state coverage, not silently describe one chosen instance.

nodes.label: Self-contained deployable artifacts
nodes.rationale: Each separately deployed component has one artifact with content-based identity and fixed provenance.

nodes.label: Pre-service configuration validation
nodes.rationale: One schema-driven pass reports every invalid or missing item before any surface accepts traffic.

nodes.label: Operator-supplied root material
nodes.rationale: Root key material is supplied outside the platform and validated before service.

nodes.label: Installation-wide observability
nodes.rationale: Probes, signals, outcomes, and audit records expose state across instances with explicit coverage.

nodes.label: Stuck exchange diagnostics
nodes.rationale: One operational query from any instance distinguishes absence, stall, and partition without requiring the sidecar or backend.

nodes.label: Sidecar registry inspection
nodes.rationale: The registry reports eligible entries, holding instance, negotiated version, capabilities, liveness, drain and load.

nodes.label: End-to-end sidecar liveness
nodes.rationale: An open transport socket does not prove that sidecar contract logic can respond.

nodes.label: Operator exchange and tunnel actions
nodes.rationale: An operator can terminate one exchange or drain or disconnect one tunnel, with attribution and unambiguous failure.

nodes.label: Deferred human-facing control plane
nodes.rationale: The v1 operational endpoint is machine-shaped while the human-facing plane is deferred.

nodes.label: Operator principal ownership gap
nodes.rationale: No current capability specifies issuance, authentication, or scope of an operator principal.

nodes.label: Audit retention conflict
nodes.rationale: Append-only audit and unstated retention policy require a decision on redaction, tombstoning, or refusal.

nodes.label: Per-tenant bound value origin gap
nodes.rationale: Bounds are enforced and observable but their configured values have no owning capability.

nodes.label: Migration action surface gap
nodes.rationale: Migration actions assume an operational surface whose definition is deferred.

nodes.label: Protocol fidelity
nodes.rationale: Protocol support follows from preserving shared properties, especially irreversible wire-contract fields, rather than protocol-specific branches.

nodes.label: Opaque octet-stream bodies
nodes.rationale: Binary bodies must remain octets, not be coerced through JSON strings.

nodes.label: Ordered repeatable header fields
nodes.rationale: An ordered sequence preserves repeated Set-Cookie fields and field-line order.

nodes.label: Open-ended method tokens
nodes.rationale: Methods pass unchanged except narrowly specified CONNECT and TRACE edge handling.

nodes.label: Raw request target
nodes.rationale: Scheme, authority, path, query and extended CONNECT protocol stay distinct; encoded segment content survives.

nodes.label: Reserved frame vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Frame types need reservation before tenants pin sidecar versions.

nodes.label: Stream IDs and credit windows
nodes.rationale: Frame headers reserve flow control and multiplexing fields.

nodes.label: Capability negotiation and refusal
nodes.rationale: Declared capability sets gate eligibility and unsupported traffic is refused.

nodes.label: Request affinity key
nodes.rationale: Stateful polling, WebDAV locks, and Digest nonces may need the same sidecar.

nodes.label: Incremental streaming and backpressure
nodes.rationale: Bounded frames and end-to-end credit prevent slow clients from accumulating unbounded memory.

nodes.label: Fair per-stream multiplexing
nodes.rationale: Bounded interleaved frames prevent a large transfer from starving small exchanges or liveness.

nodes.label: Cancellation and RESET propagation
nodes.rationale: Client abandonment must cancel backend work and reconnect must not replay non-idempotent calls.

nodes.label: Timeout taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Distinct connect, first-byte, idle, total and edge-header timers accommodate long-lived streams.

nodes.label: Distinct trailer sections
nodes.rationale: Trailers follow body frames and remain separate from initial headers.

nodes.label: Interim responses
nodes.rationale: A stream may carry 1xx sections before one final response; 100-continue requires early header forwarding.

nodes.label: Range request fidelity
nodes.rationale: Partial content and open-ended ranges serve media seeking without whole-response buffering.

nodes.label: WebSocket session fidelity
nodes.rationale: Deferred 101, ordering, frame shape, and close codes preserve session semantics.

nodes.label: Server-Sent Events
nodes.rationale: A response can stay open for hours while events flush incrementally.

nodes.label: Long-polling request class
nodes.rationale: A backend deliberately holds the request before responding.

nodes.label: Graceful stream drain
nodes.rationale: Routine upgrades must avoid synchronized disconnect and reconnect storms.

nodes.label: Per-tenant stream quotas
nodes.rationale: Long-lived streams require admission against occupancy and buffered bytes.

nodes.label: Sidecar gRPC-Web bridge
nodes.rationale: The sidecar is adjacent to HTTP/2 backends and can bridge browser-compatible gRPC-Web.

nodes.label: WebDAV family
nodes.rationale: Open method and target fidelity plus streaming support WebDAV without new tunnel primitives.

nodes.label: WebTransport deferral
nodes.rationale: WebTransport is reserved in the contract for a later separate terminator because edge termination is the blocker.

nodes.label: Domain ownership verification
nodes.rationale: Issuing a certificate after an unverified claim could obtain one for another party's domain.

nodes.label: Outbound sidecar dial
nodes.rationale: The backend needs no inbound network path because the sidecar dials outward.

nodes.label: Inspectable sidecar artifact
nodes.rationale: A tenant platform team can assess configuration, compatibility, dependencies, and identity before running it.

nodes.label: Declared configuration schema
nodes.rationale: The schema is the single enumeration of sidecar configuration values; note-local names would drift.

nodes.label: Fail-fast configuration validation
nodes.rationale: Validation must report all faults before touching the credential, endpoint, or backend.

nodes.label: Tenant-local diagnostics
nodes.rationale: The tenant cannot inspect the proxy and must diagnose a stuck tunnel from its own infrastructure.

nodes.label: Capability refusal
nodes.rationale: A sidecar declares what its build and configuration can do so unsupported routes fail explicitly.

nodes.label: Artifact distribution and update notification gap
nodes.norm_label: artifact distribution and update notification gap

nodes.label: Client, tenant, and operator viewpoints
nodes.rationale: The same failure is observed differently across three network and trust positions.

nodes.label: Privacy-driven diagnostic asymmetry
nodes.rationale: Unauthenticated peers must not learn capacity or credential-state details.

nodes.label: Six independent timeout bounds
nodes.rationale: A single request timeout cannot account for long-lived or multi-hop exchanges.

nodes.label: Partitioned stream and tunnel error codes
nodes.norm_label: partitioned stream and tunnel error codes

nodes.label: Silence failure class
nodes.rationale: A traffic failure outside the supported surface may appear successful before silently stalling.

nodes.label: Frames carrying stream IDs
nodes.rationale: Independent stream IDs replace the reference correlation-ID map and allow exchanges to interleave.

nodes.label: V1 frame vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Reserve frame kinds in v1 because adding them later splits a permanently skewed fleet.

nodes.label: Per-stream credit windows
nodes.rationale: Credit windows supply backpressure absent from the previous attempt.

nodes.label: HTTP/2 WebTransport capsule option
nodes.rationale: A standard capsule format could provide framing and conformance targets, but server-library availability is unresolved.

nodes.label: Tunnel capability negotiation
nodes.rationale: A declared capability set prevents identical requests from differing with sidecar version.

nodes.label: Deferred WebSocket handshake
nodes.rationale: The tunnel open should return the backend handshake before the edge replies 101.

nodes.label: WebSocket frame fidelity
nodes.rationale: FIN, RSV, opcode, ordering, and application close codes must survive.

nodes.label: Per-hop WebSocket heartbeat
nodes.rationale: Ping and pong are handled per hop, so end-to-end liveness needs its own mechanism.

nodes.label: Compression as tenant-isolation concern
nodes.rationale: A compressed frame can inflate enough to exhaust a shared node.

nodes.label: Go edge terminator
nodes.rationale: A separate contract speaker supplies HTTP/2 and makes future edge protocols swappable.

nodes.label: Elixir proxy runtime
nodes.rationale: WebTransport does not force HTTP/3 termination in the same process; BEAM suits routing and registry work.

nodes.label: Go sidecar runtime
nodes.rationale: A static binary and familiar HTTP/TLS stack fit tenant deployment.

nodes.label: Per-hop framing authority
nodes.rationale: Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding belong to each connection and both together are a smuggling surface.

nodes.label: Proxy traffic before application middleware
nodes.rationale: Application middleware caused the reference to lose POST bodies.

nodes.label: Request/response byte stream
nodes.rationale: Nine named protocols differ only by content type or method token and use one opaque HTTP stream.

nodes.label: Bidirectional frame stream
nodes.rationale: WebSocket-derived protocols require ordered, binary-safe, frame-shaped traffic.

nodes.label: QUIC streams and unreliable datagrams
nodes.rationale: WebTransport is reserved in the contract and deferred.

nodes.label: Out-of-scope protocol families
nodes.rationale: WebRTC media, Web Push with VAPID, and NTLM do not fit these proxy primitives.

nodes.label: Undeclared correspondence drift
nodes.rationale: Published and computed enumerations can diverge while a gate remains green.

nodes.label: CODEOWNERS review blocking gap
nodes.rationale: One maintainer cannot approve their own PR; requiring review would prevent merging.

nodes.label: Configuration/provenance name collision verification
nodes.rationale: The real configuration schema is needed before the collision can be demonstrated.

nodes.label: make check latency
nodes.rationale: The meta-gate cross-product grows quadratically and slow feedback weakens test quality.

nodes.label: Credential and key-custody specification link gap
nodes.norm_label: credential and key-custody specification link gap

nodes.label: CORS and WHIP Location visibility gap
nodes.norm_label: cors and whip location visibility gap

nodes.label: Archived and live spec glob overlap
nodes.norm_label: archived and live spec glob overlap

nodes.label: The harness and its findings
nodes.rationale: Structural checks and adversarial verification constrain the failure modes observed in the previous attempt.

nodes.label: Documentation rules
nodes.rationale: Documentation must be falsifiable and change with behaviour; orientation links to the owning contract.

nodes.label: Conventions for authoring a note
nodes.rationale: Fifteen conventions are enforced by named gates and delivered to both authoring channels.

nodes.label: Supply chain, changelog and versioning
nodes.rationale: The wire contract and software have independent version streams because tenant sidecars can remain old.

nodes.label: Authority precedence
nodes.rationale: Higher authority resolves conflicts: contract, specifications, decisions, spine notes, then generated indexes.

nodes.label: Method index
nodes.rationale: Generated navigation index for method notes.

nodes.label: Published and computed enumerations reconcile
nodes.rationale: Independently encoded sets require declared correspondence checked in both directions.

nodes.label: Gate coverage is an assertion
nodes.rationale: Coverage reports count subjects actually examined and identify their source.

nodes.label: Method rules index
nodes.rationale: Generated navigation index for method rule notes.

nodes.label: Every blocking gate runs
nodes.rationale: A tracked runner invokes the aggregating target on every declared trigger and propagates failure.

nodes.label: Violating inputs declare their failures
nodes.rationale: Each violating tree declares expected failures and counts for verification against actual gate output.

nodes.label: Generated artifacts have an oracle
nodes.rationale: Generators are checked against small tracked inputs and independently pinned expected outputs.

nodes.label: Cited artifacts are obtainable
nodes.rationale: Citations resolve to tracked or revision-pinned obtainable artifacts, with absent prior art reported as unverifiable.

nodes.label: Declared scanners are invoked
nodes.rationale: Scanners appear in executable workflow positions on every declared trigger, including weekly runs.

nodes.label: One obligation has consistent invocations
nodes.rationale: Independent invocations of one obligation use the same flags and standing checks run periodically.

nodes.label: Conventions reach both authoring channels
nodes.rationale: The planning configuration and generated note share one convention enumeration and must agree.

nodes.label: Spine notes defer owned behaviour
nodes.rationale: A note summarising specified behaviour marks it non-normative and links the owning specification.

nodes.label: Entry files route and stay small
nodes.rationale: Entry files link into the vault, state invariants and banned patterns, and name only present artifacts.
nodes.norm_label: entry files route and stay small

nodes.label: Currency runs in both directions
nodes.rationale: Planned markers appear before implementation and retire when their subject or task is complete.

nodes.label: Requirement text has one copy
nodes.rationale: The spine, specifications and components link to one requirement text instead of duplicating it.

nodes.label: Every gate is demonstrated to fail
nodes.rationale: Each gate must reject its own violating fixture by its own logic.
nodes.norm_label: every gate is demonstrated to fail

nodes.label: Every note is reachable
nodes.rationale: Notes and planning artifacts must be reachable from an entry point, with planning artifacts linked from notes.

nodes.label: Every capability has a concept note
nodes.rationale: Specifications and concept notes correspond one to one, and every dependency is linked from its capability note.
nodes.norm_label: every capability has a concept note

nodes.label: Every tracked note lives under a declared root
nodes.rationale: The root set is closed and each root is governed or explicitly exempt.
nodes.norm_label: every tracked note lives under a declared root

nodes.label: Reader settings are tracked
nodes.rationale: Link resolution and note classification settings are tracked and value checked; personal UI state is excluded.

nodes.label: Out-of-scope artifacts stay byte unchanged
nodes.rationale: A gate enforces an explicit change boundary in the normal gate run.

nodes.label: Relations are relative Markdown links
nodes.rationale: One link syntax is readable by people, agents, and checkers.

nodes.label: Every link resolves, anchors included
nodes.rationale: Missing files and missing anchors are distinguished and reported together.

nodes.label: Exactly one decision register
nodes.rationale: Unnamespaced decision identifiers belong only in the declared register; retired IDs are not reused.

nodes.label: Every note carries a classification
nodes.rationale: Notes declare type, status, and authority from closed enumerations; spine notes are not normative.

nodes.label: Generated indexes cannot drift
nodes.rationale: A generated, tracked index must equal fresh regeneration byte for byte.

nodes.label: Multi-tenant platform ingress
nodes.rationale: The operator runs the ingress path and the tenant is a first-class entity; this is the comparison axis.

nodes.label: ngrok
nodes.rationale: Runs a globally distributed ingress service and carries general TCP endpoints and traffic policy.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Tunnel
nodes.rationale: Outbound tunnel that sends traffic through Cloudflare network.

nodes.label: frp
nodes.rationale: Self-hosted reverse proxy with client-declared routes, TCP and UDP support, and shared-token authentication.

nodes.label: Tailscale Funnel
nodes.rationale: Exposes a service on a device in a private tailnet; constrained to tailnet DNS names and specific ports.

nodes.label: Dynamic-configuration reverse proxy
nodes.rationale: Caddy and Traefik change routes without restarts; route source and connection direction differ from Plugboard.

nodes.label: Operator success criteria
nodes.rationale: Isolation, predictable failure, a single ordered audit trail, and tenant-independent upgrades must be demonstrable.

nodes.label: Contributor success criteria
nodes.rationale: A clean-clone development command, fast offline test tier, independent conformance suite, and fixture-backed first issues are measurable.

nodes.label: Portfolio success criteria
nodes.rationale: The decision register should expose rationale, reversals, costs, refusals, and stable citations.

nodes.label: Checkable criteria
nodes.rationale: A criterion must name an observation and an artifact that decides it.

nodes.label: WebRTC media and data channel refusal
nodes.rationale: Ephemeral UDP, ICE, SRTP, and SCTP-over-DTLS call for a TURN relay with different economics; control-plane HTTP and WebSocket remain supported.
nodes.norm_label: webrtc media and data channel refusal

nodes.label: Web Push with VAPID
nodes.rationale: Push traffic goes from tenant application to a push service and does not traverse Plugboard.

nodes.label: NTLM and SPNEGO refusal
nodes.rationale: Connection-bound multi-round-trip authentication cannot be expressed by independent multiplexed tunnel streams.

nodes.label: TLS passthrough refusal
nodes.rationale: Encrypted Client Hello hides the routing field required by this mode.

nodes.label: Full gRPC ingress refusal
nodes.rationale: The remaining refusal is scope; the original trailer-based reason was retired by the HTTP/2 terminator decision.

nodes.label: Response cache refusal
nodes.rationale: No v1 cache means no cache-key design or cache-poisoning surface.

nodes.label: Health-probe load balancing refusal
nodes.rationale: Sidecar selection uses registry membership and liveness, without active probes.

nodes.label: WebTransport deferral
nodes.rationale: Reserved in the contract for a later HTTP/3 terminator.

nodes.label: HTTP/3 edge deferral
nodes.rationale: The edge terminator can add HTTP/3 without changing the tunnel.

nodes.label: WHIP/WHEP and Connect deferral
nodes.rationale: Later support uses frame types already reserved in the contract.

nodes.label: WHIP browser CORS gap
nodes.rationale: No specification currently owns CORS or Access-Control-Expose-Headers for browser WHIP clients.

nodes.label: Permanent asymmetric version skew
nodes.rationale: The operator deploys the proxy; tenants deploy sidecars whenever or never.

nodes.label: Irreversible wire schema
nodes.rationale: Old sidecars remain in production, so a later schema fix cannot reach them.

nodes.label: Capability negotiation
nodes.rationale: Round-robin sidecar selection otherwise gives identical requests different fidelity across versions.

nodes.label: Permanent sidecar change cost
nodes.rationale: Any change requiring tenant deployment remains expensive indefinitely.

nodes.label: Plugboard dynamic ingress
nodes.rationale: Applications register routing at runtime over persistent outbound tunnels; designed for multi-tenant platforms.

nodes.label: Outbound sidecar tunnel
nodes.rationale: Telephone dials Plugboard and relays traffic to a local tenant backend.

nodes.label: Runtime mount points
nodes.rationale: Database-backed mount points are projected into memory, allowing route changes without restarts.

nodes.label: Registration is the deploy
nodes.rationale: Live sidecar membership makes a backend routable without external service-discovery configuration.

nodes.label: Tenant custom domains
nodes.rationale: Tenants use their own hostnames after an ownership check.

nodes.label: Three project audiences
nodes.rationale: Operator, contributor, and portfolio requirements conflict; operators set hard requirements.

nodes.label: Platform operators
nodes.rationale: Buyers want tenant isolation, predictable failure, an audit trail, and boring upgrades.

nodes.label: Contributors
nodes.rationale: Want fast setup and tests, small reviewable units, and clear module boundaries.

nodes.label: Author portfolio
nodes.rationale: Wants legible, defensible decisions; written rationale mitigates over-engineering.

nodes.label: Operator tie-break
nodes.rationale: The tenant-isolation promise makes tenant scoping a schema decision from day one.

nodes.label: Proxy
nodes.rationale: Operator-run Elixir application for routing, registry, tenant state, and tunnel endpoint.

nodes.label: Edge terminator
nodes.rationale: Go contract speaker that terminates client HTTP/2 in v1 and later HTTP/3 with WebTransport.

hyperedges.label: One wire contract across all implementations
